verdict.rationale: Fly.io's Sprites give each agent its own Linux box. The docs say a Sprite checkpoints itself automatically while the agent works and keeps a durable filesystem, so agents like Claude and Codex find their state where they left it. Sprites sleep, wake 'remembering everything', and can roll back to any checkpoint in seconds. missing for 10: in-depth technical docs on checkpoint frequency, scope and retention (the evidence is mostly homepage marketing copy), and independent or hands-on corroboration of Sprite checkpointing.

support.subject: As an ai-native builder, I can give my coding agent a persistent runtime environment that checkpoints its state automatically while working

citations.quote: A Sprite checkpoints itself while the agent works, so harnesses like Claude and Codex find everything where they left it.
Give it a Sprite that sleeps until it's needed and wakes up remembering everything.
Roll back to any checkpoint in seconds
They appear instantly, always include durable filesystems, and cost practically nothing when idle.
